correctness.rationale: The Fano-plane incidence model has 21 flags. Four flags cannot form an induced matching (four selected Fano points have no four respective tangent lines), so maximum induced-matching size is three. Independently enumerating all C(21,3)=1330 flags triples gives exactly 84 compatible triples. A least-uncovered-flag exact-cover recursion enumerates all 416 unordered partitions into seven triples, without duplicates. Independent pair comparison gives no two-class trade and exactly 1568 three-class trade edges. Complete BFS from each of 416 vertices gives connectedness and eccentricity exactly 6; degree counts 112 of degree5, 280 of degree8, 24 of degree14. Source verifier also constructs 168 collineations plus duality, with claimed 336 actions and six orbits 8,16,56,112,112,112; group orbit figures were inspected in source but not separately recomputed in independent checker. This is a natural finite exhaustive classification, not a sample.

evidence: Kloks et al. arXiv:1110.3583 graph-class algorithms exclude exact Heawood reconfiguration census.
Luzar et al. arXiv:2101.04768 discusses strong edge colorings and known Heawood chromatic index seven.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A general chromatic-index or constructive existence theorem does not determine the full optimal-solution graph or eccentricities. Petersen uniqueness is a different graph.

This sharp finite threshold and six-step diameter is mathematically meaningful even without a general theorem for all cubic graphs.
